correctness.rationale: For 0<p<=1 the p-th quasi-triangle inequality on singular-value expansions bounds any input by its rank-one factors; testing rank-one factors gives equality. Orthogonal rotations reduce every masked rank-one xy* to B_(s,t)=[[sqrt(st),sqrt(s(1-t))],[sqrt((1-s)t),0]], whose singular-value squared sum is s+t-st and product sqrt(st(1-s)(1-t)). At fixed s+t increasing st decreases its largest singular value while strictly increasing a+b; since p<=1 the sum a^p+b^p strictly grows, attaining s=t. The k=sqrt(u/(4-3u)) derivative G(k)+H_p(k) has G decreasing and H_p strictly decreasing for p<1, with precisely one interior zero before 1/sqrt3; for p=1 it vanishes at 1/sqrt3. The formulas give the claimed sharp norm and extremizing rank-one projection; finite independent s,t tests and the p=1,1/2 endpoint algebra passed.
residual_risks: The p<1 Banach-space triangle inequality must be replaced with its quasi-norm p-th power form; the proof uses this correct variant.
Finite-dimensional tests do not prove the infinite-dimensional singular-value expansion; completeness in S_p and p-subadditivity supply it.

value.rationale: The three-one 2-by-2 cross is the smallest genuinely nontrivial Schur idempotent. Its exact sharp quasi-Schatten norm as a function of the exponent, its optimizer and trace-class endpoint supply a natural operator-ideal invariant omitted from qualitative support classifications. It is not merely verification that the pattern is bounded.
residual_risks: Only one distinguished row and column; extension to multiple rows or p>1 is not claimed.

limitations: Original unmodified result survives; no claim for p>1 or multirow masks.
